assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: Split into the two possibilities for the generated ideal I=(g_1,...,g_d). The full-ideal branch is isolated as an explicit bottleneck lemma. In the proper-ideal branch, finite-dimensionality forces I to be m-primary, so S/I has Krull dimension 0. Independently, the weighted polynomial ring has Krull dimension d and is Cohen-Macaulay. Therefore the general proper-ideal Cohen-Macaulay regularity theorem applies to g_1,...,g_d and gives the successive non-zero-divisor property. Finally, combine the two branches and translate that property into the phrase 'homogeneous regular sequence'.

assembly_plan.proof_skeleton_nl: First split off the branch where the generated ideal is the whole ring; that exceptional case is isolated as an explicit bottleneck. In the proper-ideal branch, finite-dimensionality implies the ideal is m-primary, so after localizing at m=(x_1,...,x_d) the quotient has finite length. Properness plus homogeneity also forces every generator to lie in m. The local ring S_m is regular local of dimension d, so the localized sequence g_1/1,...,g_d/1 is regular by the regular-local criterion. Localization-quotient compatibility then identifies the localized successive quotients, and a graded local-to-global injectivity lemma descends injectivity from each localized quotient back to the original graded quotient. Finally combine the two branches and rewrite the result as the statement that g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.

semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: The successive non-zero-divisor condition for g_1,...,g_d is equivalent to saying that g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence.
quantifier_order: Given a positively graded commutative ring S and homogeneous elements g_1,...,g_d of S

lemmas.statement_nl: Let S be a positively graded commutative ring, and let g_1,...,g_d be homogeneous elements of S. Then the condition that for every i with 1 <= i <= d, the image of g_i in S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is not a zero-divisor is exactly the statement that g_1,...,g_d is a homogeneous regular sequence, under the convention that regularity means injectivity of each multiplication map on the successive quotients.
lemmas.strictly_easier_reason: This only unpacks terminology and does not contribute new commutative-algebra content.

shared_context.content: S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with deg(x_i) = w_i for positive integers w_i; homogeneity always refers to this weighted grading.
shared_context.label: Weighted polynomial ring

shared_context.content: m = (x_1,...,x_d) is the homogeneous maximal ideal of S.
shared_context.label: Irrelevant maximal ideal

shared_context.content: S_m denotes the localization of S at the complement of m.
shared_context.label: Localization at m

shared_context.content: A sequence g_1,...,g_d of homogeneous elements of a graded ring is called a homogeneous regular sequence if for every i with 1 <= i <= d, multiplication by the image of g_i on S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is injective; equivalently, that image is not a zero-divisor there.
shared_context.label: Homogeneous regular sequence

full_candidate.strategy_summary: Local regular-ring strategy: isolate the full-ideal branch as a bottleneck, and in the proper-ideal branch localize at the homogeneous maximal ideal m=(x_1,...,x_d). Finite-dimensionality makes the localized quotient finite length, S_m is regular local of dimension d, so the localized sequence is regular. Then descend injectivity from the localization back to the original graded quotients using a graded local-to-global injectivity lemma.

previous_attempt_summaries.vet_summary: The decomposition fails because L1 is false, and in fact the root theorem is false as stated. A concrete counterexample is S = k[x_1,x_2] with g_1 = 0 and g_2 = 1: then S/(g_1,g_2)=0 is finite-dimensional, but g_1 is a zero-divisor on S. Apart from this fatal issue, the proper-ideal/localization branch is plausibly correct and the assembly is conditionally coherent.

shared_context.content: For a field k, a nonnegative integer d, and positive integers w_1,...,w_d, write S = k[x_1,...,x_d] and grade it by deg(x_i)=w_i. Homogeneous always refers to this weighted grading.
shared_context.label: Weighted polynomial ring

shared_context.content: m = (x_1,...,x_d) is the homogeneous maximal ideal of S.
shared_context.label: Homogeneous maximal ideal

shared_context.content: For any S-module M, write M_m for the localization of M at the multiplicative set S \ m. In particular S_m is the localization of S at S \ m.
shared_context.label: Localization at m

shared_context.content: A sequence g_1,...,g_d of homogeneous elements in a positively graded ring S is a homogeneous regular sequence if for each i with 1 <= i <= d, multiplication by the image of g_i on S/(g_1,...,g_{i-1}) is injective. For d=0 this means the empty sequence, which is regular by convention.
shared_context.label: Homogeneous regular sequence
